description: The next production candidate, tp4/next-1: the approved ship-4 profile (traffic-s4, unchanged and its waiver untouched) plus the lone-user padded round (NP1), exact resume P0, the sliced host-tier restore and the decode verify sub-switch of the 13x10 grids, the device-side hand-off of the final prefill step (PF2-H), the lean admission and the complete spills of the scheduler levers, with the owner-approved host RAM budget (a 48 GiB tier beside a 16 GiB checkpoint store), as ONE traffic profile under ONE owner traffic waiver (decision PENDING; the owner approves at ship time). The Swift catalog entry also carries the 32,768-token output ceiling (NP9) for every Swift boot of the image. Its audited twin (-s5-audit: every audit of the shipped levers and of the merged ones, the W3 WC lever with its audit) is generated by make_s5_profiles.py; its window packs are references/fusion-jobs/S5 (make_s5_jobs.py). W3 MR and W3 keyed are not in this tree: the batched reads and the round-host keyed diff of the shipped stack are the same levers (docs/tp4-next1.md).

ship.reason: the NEXT production candidate (tp4/next-1) on the shipped ship-4 stack: the approved ship-4 profile plus the lone-user padded round (NP1), exact resume P0 (the undrop and the drafter-window carry), the sliced host-tier restore, the decode verify sub-switch of the 13x10 matmul grids (QWEN_FAST_GRID13=1), the device-side hand-off of the final prefill step's GDN state (PF2-H), the lean admission and the complete spills (sched-1), and the owner-approved host RAM budget (a 48 GiB tier beside a 16 GiB checkpoint store), under ONE owner traffic waiver (decision PENDING). The W3 levers are not in it. Its exactness control is the approved ship-4 profile on the same image

(owner traffic waiver <id>)" line once. PF2-H: "[PINDIAG] prefill handoff engaged" once, "[PF2] handoff mode=device ms=.. read_ms=.. write_ms=.." on every final step, no "fell back" line, and in the audited run "prefill handoff audit n=.. exact=True" for every audited step and no "audit mismatch": the line ships only if the audited run passes. SCHED-1: python3 scripts/ci/sched_report.py <container log> on the A1 and both T1 logs (the rebind p50 and p90, the lean split and phases, the read-backs skipped, the backstop reuses, the spill fit and counters; every figure prints - where no line is behind it); the lean lines in the log, and the complete-spill mode's install line with its default knobs. waiver.waives: ONE waiver for everything the NEXT production candidate (tp4/next-1, the ship-5 candidate) carries that has no pinned qualification record. It carries, unchanged, every item the approved ship-4 waiver (ship4-fx-262k-2026-10-11, approved by the owner 2026-10-12) waives, EXCEPT the three changes (C2), (E2) and (L) named after it, and adds five levers, (G) to (K). THE INHERITED TEXT, verbatim from the ship-4 waiver: ONE waiver for everything this production candidate carries that has no pinned qualification record, each lever named with what it is outside of. (A) Inherited in full from w2-er-fx-262k-2026-10-11 (the approved fusion ship waiver, docs/tp4-fusion.md): the W2 multi SDPA launch (QWEN_FAST_TP4_SDPA=multi: outside packed_any_evidence_tp4_262144.json) and F1 (QWEN_FAST_TP4_CONV_GATES_SPREAD=1: no record), engine reuse and its drafter-trace book (QWEN_FAST_PARKED_ENGINES, QWEN_FAST_PARKED_DRAFTS: no ballast ladder, kill-switch drill or fault job), and the op-fusion levers (default-off, exact by construction and by audit on cards, no contract mechanism: named as the owner's decision). (B) The octo shape and its three levers, (1) QWEN_FAST_OCTO=live, the third packed block of eight users of eight rows (one 64-row verify pass instead of two M3 passes at eight live seats): its attention is the K64j extent program at flags 0x21 with one eight-row group per bundle (geometry G8B1), which is outside the pinned four-card evidence records (packed_any_evidence_tp4.json and packed_any_evidence_tp4_262144.json cover the served G8B2 programs at flags 0x23 and the multi-user launch is the M3 blocks' own), the batched GDN launch at eight users (96 cores, one wave) has no card-M record, and the serving_octo admission refuses the shape outside a gate run of a gate-only profile (QWEN_C2_GATE=1 with QWEN_C2_GATE_PROFILE=1) - this waiver is the one other way in, named by the profile's own QWEN_FAST_OCTO_WAIVER; (2) QWEN_FAST_OCTO_ATTN_BUNDLE=4, the octo block's attention in two K64j launches of four users per layer (flags 0x21 with B > 1 entries, 16 cores per entry, no kernel or factory change), outside every record; (3) QWEN_FAST_OCTO_GLUE8=1, the GDN split, merge, block conv and packed windows run by quarter-tile data-movement kernels at eight-row users (exact by construction and by the in-trace audit of the audited attach, with no card-M mover harness and no pinned record); (4) QWEN_FAST_OCTO_DRAFT=1, one eight-seat, eight-row draft pass in place of the two quads for an all-eight-live octo round (it can change only how many tokens a round commits (tau: its checkpoint is trained at sixteen rows), never which, and its trace beside engine reuse is not in the draft book: the coordinator rebuilds it after a rebound member); and QWEN_FAST_OCTO_MIN_LIVE=6, the eligibility knob. A record could replace this waiver: the K64j card jobs Q1w, Q1a and Q1b (k64j_card_b.py --kv-heads 1 --octo: G8B1 at flags 0x21 equal to its compile-time twin at every family and start, one trace over more than 50 families, the stale-writer zone and the native one-row decode against the one-entry call) with a bundle arm for B = 4 (not built), Q2 (gdn_tp4_card_test.py --users 8 --rows 8: one launch equal to eight per-user launches bit for bit) and a quarter-tile mover harness (not built), recorded in a new pinned section of the packed-any evidence beside the G8B2 one (not built); until then the owner's decision stands in for them. The op-fusion levers and QWEN_FAST_TAP_WINDOW_ALIGNED this profile also sets are the fusion ship waiver's kind (default-off, exact by construction and by audit, no contract mechanism) and are inherited from w2-er-fx-262k-2026-10-11 and named here as the owner's decision, not as a mechanism. (C) The host KV tier and the preconverted GDN checkpoints (QWEN_PREFIX_HOST_TIER_GIB=32 beside the 8 GiB checkpoint store, QWEN_PREFIX_CKPT_PRECONVERTED=1; docs/prefix-store-hygiene.md): outside any pinned record (the contract, prefix_policy_problems, admits them on a traffic profile only under a waiver naming each at this value, TIER_WAIVABLE_LEVERS); exact on cards on the gate-only audit twins, but the tier has run beside no concurrent decode of other seats, and never beside octo-T8, engine reuse's rebind of a parked engine on a restored turn, or the 16,500-block pool. The per-tenant quotas (QWEN_PREFIX_TENANT_QUOTA_*) are NOT in this profile: the contract refuses them on traffic (no qualification record exists) and the quota isolation gate TQ1 runs them on the audit twin only. (D) The prefill SDPA with one q chunk per core (QWEN_FAST_SDPA_PF_ONEQ=1): default-off, byte-identical to the stock path by the card-M proof and by audit; its binary K64j-OQ differs from the one the older packed-any records were made on and its OWN records have landed (RQ0-RQ2, all PASS), so a traffic boot passes admission; named here as the owner's decision. (E) The matmul grids for the 13x10 grid (QWEN_FAST_GRID13=prefill,drafter, M1): default-off, exact by argument and by audit on cards for the two sub-switches this profile names, the prefill all-gather matmuls and the fused commit's drafter feature projection. The third sub-switch, verify (the 64-row verify block's output projections, site verify.out), is NOT in this profile: its first audited attach (card run 38116769673) stopped at engine start before it compared anything, so it has never been audited exact on a card; it stays in the audited twin -s4-audit, whose next attach exercises and audits it, and adding it to the candidate (QWEN_FAST_GRID13=1) is a later decision after that audit passes. The decode ABAB of the grids (the F2 window) had not reported when this was written, so the line is the one switchable line of this profile: delete it from the ship entry of scripts/ci/fusion-wp/S4.json (and regenerate) if that ABAB or the N1/N2 pair shows a loss. (F) QWEN_FAST_TAP_WINDOW_ALIGNED=1 (tp4/rebind-fast: data movement only, bit-identical, removes a per-prompt-length compile on returning turns) and the tool-call whitespace fix (c2_toolcall_whitespace, a correctness fix, default ON for every profile, not a lever) are named as the owner's decision. Nothing in this list has run on a card TOGETHER: the audited attach A1, the ship gates and the tier pair of references/fusion-jobs/ship4 are the first CHANGES TO THE INHERITED ITEMS. (C2) The host KV tier is raised from the ship-4 waiver's 32 GiB beside the 8 GiB checkpoint store to QWEN_PREFIX_HOST_TIER_GIB=48 beside QWEN_PREFIX_STORE_GIB=16 (the whole prefix state's host budget: a 32 GiB share for the attention-KV pages and 16 GiB for the checkpoints, the budget the owner approved for this candidate; the preconverted checkpoints are unchanged: QWEN_PREFIX_CKPT_PRECONVERTED=1). The tier's mechanism is the one the ship-4 waiver's evidence covers; the size is the new number, and the larger checkpoint store is what the drafter-window carry (H) needs (each checkpoint then also holds up to 105 MB of window rows). (E2) QWEN_FAST_GRID13=1 in place of =prefill,drafter: the third sub-switch, verify (the 64-row verify block's output projections, site verify.out), joins the two the ship-4 waiver names. The ship-4 waiver held it out because its first audited attach had stopped at engine start before comparing anything; the ship-4 audited attach A1 (the audited twin carries QWEN_FAST_GRID13=1, all three sub-switches) has since compared it, exact on every audited round (the owner's reading: 4 of 4). It is default-off elsewhere and is the one switchable line of the candidate for this item: delete QWEN_FAST_GRID13 (or set it to prefill,drafter) in the ship entry of scripts/ci/fusion-wp/S5.json and regenerate if a timed pair shows a loss. (L) QWEN_FAST_OCTO_WAIVER names THIS waiver's id (the one name by which a non-gate run admits the octo shape and the lone-user round). ADDITIONS. (G) The lone-user padded round, QWEN_FAST_SOLO_PACKED=1 (NP1, docs/tp4-np1-fastlane.md): a lone live user (and a lone user of either M3 block) decodes on the padded 64-row packed block instead of its own 4-row engine; its third idle segment writes a scratch KV block the model's allocation adds past vLLM's pool (557,056 bytes a chip, idle_scratch.py). Gate-only until now (the contract refused it on a traffic profile and the admission ran in a gate run only): this waiver is the one other way in, as for octo-T8. No kernel, program or trace is new; what no card has done is give the K/V writers and the extent reader a block id past the pool in a page table (docs/tp4-np1-fastlane.md section 6, K1 to K4). Exactness is argued (the live segment's rows do not depend on where the idle segments write) and held by CPU tests; its audits run in the audited twin. (H) Exact resume P0, QWEN_PREFIX_STICKY_UNDROP=1 and QWEN_PREFIX_WINDOW_CARRY=1 (docs/tp4-exact-resume.md): a returning sticky turn resumes at floor2048(P) instead of floor2048(P) - 2048 (vLLM's last-block drop is lifted for the hit lookup, and the drafter window rows below the checkpoint are filed on it and uploaded on the resumed turn); byte-exact by construction (the same chunk-program checkpoints one chunk higher; the cold window's own rows), gate-only until now, never run on a card; the carry's audit (QWEN_PREFIX_WINDOW_CARRY_AUDIT) stays a gate's own and is in the audited twin. The turn telemetry that comes with it is on for every profile and counts only. (I) The sliced host-tier restore, QWEN_PREFIX_TIER_RESTORE_SLICE=512 with QWEN_PREFIX_TIER_RESTORE_SLICE_MS=200 (docs/prefix-store-hygiene.md "Sliced restore"): a returning session's blocks come back from the host tier a bounded slice per engine step, the one-fresh-prefill admission wrapper holding the returning request between slices so the other seats get a round. It moves no bytes and no answer, only when the work is done; the contract admits it on a traffic profile whose waiver names the tier (this one does). Never run on a card. (J) The drafter-window carry and the sliced restore beside the tier at 48 GiB: the three have never run together or beside octo-T8 or engine reuse's concurrent seats. (K) The Swift catalog entry's output ceiling, "output_budget": 32768 (NP9, docs/tp4-np9-answer32k.md), reaches every Swift boot of the image this candidate is built into: it is data in qwen_c2_checkpoints.json, not a lever of this profile (which keeps QWEN_FAST_OUTPUT_BUDGET=16384 and a default answer of 8,192 tokens), and it is named here because the candidate ships with it: it lifts the ceiling for a client that names max_tokens above 16,384 and costs KV admission for such a request (docs/tp4-np9-answer32k.md); deleting the key restores 16,384. (M) The device-side hand-off of the final prefill step's GDN state, QWEN_FAST_PREFILL_HANDOFF=1 (PF2-H, docs/tp4-prefill-2.md): the last step of every split prompt writes the decode slot from device-side clones of the B=1 prefill scratch instead of a host round trip (240 blocking reads, 240 uploads: 48.6 ms of device idle for the reads and 115.2 ms for the writes, 8.0 ms of it device kernels, in the ship-4 stack's device profile). A clone is a bit copy of the same tensor, so the bytes written are the scratch's; a clone that fails before the first write falls back to the host path (a logged line, never a failed request). Default off, never run on a card, and not a waivable mechanism of the contract (it is named here as the owner's decision, as the op-fusion levers are). IT SHIPS ONLY IF THE AUDITED RUN PASSES: the audited twin runs it with QWEN_FAST_PREFILL_HANDOFF_AUDIT=1 (the first 8 final steps and every 24th read the whole decode state before and after the write and require the slot equal to the scratch and every other row unchanged); a mismatch or a fall-back line in the audited run takes the line out of the ship entry of scripts/ci/fusion-wp/S5.json before the owner approves. (N) The lean admission, QWEN_FAST_ADMISSION_LEAN=1 (tp4/sched-1, docs/tp4-sched-1.md): a returning turn's engine rebind skips three admission costs after a slot's first adoption (the conv-slice read-back, the 'dram after engine' line, the post-prefill backstop's allocator read when the admission's own hold reading clears it by a wide margin); the first of each stays, the DRAM hold and the backstop's terms are unchanged. It returns device time to every decoder (ESTIMATE: the sticky build p50 541 ms to about 240 ms) and trades none away. Gate-only until now; never run on a card. (O) The complete spills of the host tier, QWEN_PREFIX_HOST_TIER_SPILL_MODE=complete (sched-1, with its default knobs): a flush no longer cuts the spill at 512 blocks and drops the rest for good (87% of a 254k restore's displaced blocks in the TC1 card run), so what the sliced restore (I) displaces stays in the tier; valid only beside the tier and meant to sit beside the sliced restore, which is why it is in this candidate; the step that displaces the blocks pays for the spill (ESTIMATE 0.4 ms a block once the slab is resident). (P) QWEN_FAST_ADMISSION_DIAG_TRIM=1, an existing flag the ship-4 profile does not set: the per-admission diagnostics after the first are not taken (about 100 ms of host time inside the admission freeze); named here as the owner's decision, not as a mechanism. The sched-1 governor knobs (QWEN_FAST_LEVERN_ADAPTIVE, _OWED_CAP_MS, _SHORT_SHARE, _SHORT_WAIT_S) are NOT in this profile: they trade decoder speed for first-token time and await the owner (their gate-only arm is -sch-all). The W3 levers (WC, the GDN windows, conv and gates in one launch) are NOT in this profile: they are in the audited twin only. NOTHING in this list has run on a card together, and (G), (H), (I) have not run on a card at all: the audited attach A1 and the prefix arm A2 of references/fusion-jobs/S5 are their first.
